formats.key: addLiquidity(uint256 amount0, uint256 amount1, address to)
effects: The pool takes amount0 of zkUSD (token0) from the signer through its allowance.
The pool takes amount1 of USDC (token1) from the signer through its allowance.
The pool mints LP shares (PAR-LP) to `to`. The number comes from the reserves and the total supply, with no minimum bound.
On the first deposit, the pool keeps 1000 shares locked in itself, so `to` receives the value minus 1000.
formats.shown: Add liquidity: "Add 21.37 zkUSD and 21.37 USDC, shares to Bob", with two 'Amount' fields that carry the token and a 'To' field.

findings.title: addLiquidity does not show how many PAR-LP shares `to` receives; the pool computes it from storage.
findings.evidence: ParSwapPool.addLiquidity: `shares = Math.mulDiv(value, supply, reserve0 + reserve1);` and `_mint(to, shares);`. The descriptor has no share field, and the calldata has no minShares parameter.

findings.title: addLiquidity uses the same label 'Amount' for the zkUSD deposit and the USDC deposit.
findings.evidence: descriptor addLiquidity fields: `amount0` label "Amount" (token0) and `amount1` label "Amount" (token1). Case 0 shows 'Amount 21.37 zkUSD' and 'Amount 21.37 USDC'.
findings.fix: Change the labels to "Deposit zkUSD" and "Deposit USDC".

effects: The signer sets the allowance of `spender` over the signer's PAR-LP shares to `value`. type(uint256).max is an infinite allowance.
formats.shown: Approve LP shares: "Approve {value} PAR-LP for {spender}". At 2^255 or more the amount shows as 'Unlimited'.

formats.key: removeLiquidity(uint256 shares, uint256 minAmount0, uint256 minAmount1, address to)
effects: The pool burns `shares` PAR-LP from the signer.
`to` receives a pro-rata part of the zkUSD reserve, at least minAmount0.
`to` receives a pro-rata part of the USDC reserve, at least minAmount1.
formats.shown: Remove liquidity: "Redeem 21.37 PAR-LP to Bob", with the shares, two 'Minimum amount' fields in zkUSD and USDC, and the recipient.

findings.title: The removeLiquidity sentence 'Redeem X PAR-LP to Bob' omits the tokens received and can read like a share transfer.
findings.evidence: descriptor removeLiquidity interpolatedIntent "Redeem {shares} to {to}". The code burns the shares and sends zkUSD and USDC to `to` (`_burn(msg.sender, shares); token0.safeTransfer(to, amount0); token1.safeTransfer(to, amount1);` in _settleWithdrawal).
findings.fix: Change interpolatedIntent to "Burn {shares}, send at least {minAmount0} and {minAmount1} to {to}".

findings.title: removeLiquidity labels both minimum fields 'Minimum amount'.
findings.evidence: descriptor removeLiquidity: `minAmount0` label "Minimum amount" and `minAmount1` label "Minimum amount".
findings.fix: Change the labels to "Minimum zkUSD received" and "Minimum USDC received".

findings.title: removeLiquidity shows only lower bounds. The exact amounts out depend on the reserves in storage.
findings.evidence: ParSwapPool.removeLiquidity: `amount0 = Math.mulDiv(r0, shares, supply); amount1 = Math.mulDiv(r1, shares, supply);`

formats.key: removeLiquidityExact(uint256 amount0, uint256 amount1, uint256 maxShares, address to)
effects: The pool burns PAR-LP shares from the signer, rounded up from the reserve ratio, at most maxShares.
`to` receives exactly amount0 of zkUSD.
`to` receives exactly amount1 of USDC.
formats.shown: Remove liquidity (exact): "Withdraw {amount0} zkUSD and {amount1} USDC to {to}", with a 'Maximum shares' field ('No limit' at 2^255 or more) and the recipient.

findings.title: The removeLiquidityExact sentence omits that it burns up to maxShares of the signer's PAR-LP.
findings.evidence: descriptor removeLiquidityExact interpolatedIntent "Withdraw {amount0} and {amount1} to {to}"; code `_burn(msg.sender, shares)` with `require(shares <= maxShares)`.
findings.fix: Change interpolatedIntent to "Withdraw {amount0} and {amount1} to {to}, burn up to {maxShares}".

findings.title: removeLiquidityExact labels both withdrawal fields 'Amount', and the no-cap case renders 'No limit PAR-LP'.
findings.evidence: descriptor: `amount0` and `amount1` both have label "Amount". Case 12 shows 'Maximum shares: No limit PAR-LP'.
findings.fix: Change the labels to "Withdraw zkUSD" and "Withdraw USDC".

effects: Nothing leaves the signer.
`to` receives the pool's balance of zkUSD and USDC above the tracked reserves. Anyone can call this.
formats.shown: Skim excess: "Send excess to {to}", with the recipient.

findings.title: skim does not show the amounts swept; the pool computes them from its balances and reserves.
findings.evidence: ParSwapPool.skim: `amount0 = token0.balanceOf(address(this)) - reserve0; amount1 = token1.balanceOf(address(this)) - reserve1;`

formats.key: swap(address tokenIn, uint256 amount, address to)
effects: The pool takes `amount` of tokenIn (zkUSD or USDC) from the signer through its allowance.
`to` receives exactly `amount` of the other pool token (USDC for zkUSD, zkUSD for USDC).
formats.shown: Swap: "Swap 21.37 zkUSD, send to Bob", with 'Pay 21.37 zkUSD' and 'To Bob'. No field or sentence names the token or amount received.

findings.title: swap never shows the asset or amount the recipient receives; 'send to Bob' can read as sending zkUSD.
findings.evidence: ParSwapPool._settleSwap: `token1.safeTransfer(to, amount);` (or token0 when tokenIn is token1). descriptor swap: interpolatedIntent "Swap {amount}, send to {to}", fields only `amount` 'Pay' and `to`. Case 5 shows 'Swap 21.37 zkUSD, send to Bob', but Bob receives 21.37 USDC.
findings.fix: Add a map `otherToken` keyed by tokenIn (token0→token1, token1→token0). Add a field {"path":"amount","label":"Receive","format":"tokenAmount","params":{"token":{"map":"$.metadata.maps.otherToken","keyPath":"tokenIn"}}}. Change interpolatedIntent to say {to} receives the same amount of the other token.

formats.key: swapPushed(address tokenIn, uint256 amount, address to)
effects: Nothing leaves the signer in this call. The pool uses `amount` of tokenIn that someone already sent to it, above its reserve.
`to` receives exactly `amount` of the other pool token.
Any tokenIn surplus above `amount` stays in the pool, and anyone can skim it.
formats.shown: Swap (pre-funded): "Swap 21.37 zkUSD, send to Bob", with 'Pay 21.37 zkUSD' and 'To Bob'.

findings.title: swapPushed never shows the asset or amount the recipient receives.
findings.evidence: ParSwapPool._settleSwap: `token1.safeTransfer(to, amount);` / `token0.safeTransfer(to, amount);`. descriptor swapPushed fields: only `amount` 'Pay' (tokenIn) and `to`. Case 6 shows 'Swap 21.37 zkUSD, send to Bob'.
findings.fix: Add a 'Receive' field on `amount` with token {"map":"$.metadata.maps.otherToken","keyPath":"tokenIn"}, and name the received token in interpolatedIntent.

findings.title: swapPushed labels the input 'Pay', but this call takes nothing from the signer's wallet.
findings.evidence: ParSwapPool.swapPushed: `received = token.balanceOf(address(this)) - reserveIn; require(received >= amount)`, with no transferFrom. descriptor: `amount` label "Pay".
findings.fix: Change the label to "Already sent to pool" and the intent to "Swap tokens already sent to pool".

formats.key: swapWithAuthorization(address tokenIn, uint256 amount, address from, uint256 validAfter, uint256 validBefore, bytes32 nonce, bytes signature)
effects: The token pulls `amount` of tokenIn from `from` to the pool with `from`'s EIP-3009 receiveWithAuthorization signature. When the signer is `from`, the signer's tokens leave.
`from` receives exactly `amount` of the other pool token.
The authorization nonce is consumed in the token. A relayer submitter pays nothing.
formats.shown: Swap with authorization: "Swap 21.37 zkUSD from Alice", with 'Pay', 'From' and 'Valid before'.

findings.title: swapWithAuthorization does not show what token arrives, how much, or that `from` receives it.
findings.evidence: ParSwapPool.swapWithAuthorization: `_settleSwap(zeroForOne, amount, tokenIn, from);` which sends the other token to `from`. descriptor: interpolatedIntent "Swap {amount} from {from}"; fields Pay, From, Valid before. Case 7 shows no received asset.
findings.fix: Add a 'Receive' field on `amount` with token {"map":"$.metadata.maps.otherToken","keyPath":"tokenIn"}. Change interpolatedIntent to "Swap {amount} from {from}; {from} receives the other token".

findings.title: swapWithAuthorization hides validAfter, which is the start of the authorization window.
findings.evidence: descriptor shows only `validBefore`; ParSwapPool passes `validAfter` to `receiveWithAuthorization`.

effects: `value` PAR-LP shares leave the signer and go to `to`.

formats.key: transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 value)
effects: `value` PAR-LP shares move from `from` to `to`.
The transfer spends `value` of the signer's allowance from `from`, unless that allowance is infinite.
formats.shown: Transfer LP shares from: "Send {value} PAR-LP from {from} to {to}".

findings.format: swap(address tokenIn, uint256 amount, address to)
findings.title: swap never shows the asset or amount the recipient receives; 'send to Bob' can read as sending zkUSD.
findings.reason: The amount out always equals the amount shown (21.37), and the recipient Bob is shown in the 'To' field. The signer's zkUSD goes to the pool as shown. The only gap is the output token, which the contract picks itself as the other token of the fixed pair. That is not-critical #3 / spec-limitation, a warning at most (a map could show it), not an effect that is hidden or wrong.
findings.quote: ParSwapPool.sol _settleSwap: `token1.safeTransfer(to, amount);` / `token0.safeTransfer(to, amount);`; swap natspec: "Swap `amount` of `tokenIn` for exactly `amount` of the other token"; descriptor swap: interpolatedIntent "Swap {amount}, send to {to}", fields `amount` 'Pay' (tokenPath tokenIn) and `to` 'To'; case 5: 'Swap 21.37 zkUSD, send to Bob'.

findings.format: swapPushed(address tokenIn, uint256 amount, address to)
findings.title: swapPushed never shows the asset or amount the recipient receives.
findings.reason: Same code path as swap: exactly `amount` of the other pool token goes to `to`, and both the amount and the recipient are on screen. swapPushed also takes nothing from the signer's wallet, since it only uses tokens already pushed into the pool. Leaving out the output token is a missing value the contract works out itself (warning at most), not a critical.
findings.quote: ParSwapPool.sol swapPushed → `_settleSwap(zeroForOne, amount, tokenIn, to);` which runs `token1.safeTransfer(to, amount)` or `token0.safeTransfer(to, amount)`; descriptor swapPushed fields `amount` 'Pay' and `to` 'To'; case 6: 'Swap 21.37 zkUSD, send to Bob'.

findings.format: swapWithAuthorization(address tokenIn, uint256 amount, address from, uint256 validAfter, uint256 validBefore, bytes32 nonce, bytes signature)
findings.title: swapWithAuthorization does not show what token arrives, how much, or that `from` receives it.
findings.reason: The input comes from `from` and the output goes back to that same `from`, which is shown as 'From', at exactly the amount shown. Funds that return to the payer are not a hidden recipient (not-critical #4), and the submitter's own assets do not move. The missing output token is a warning at most.
findings.quote: ParSwapPool.sol swapWithAuthorization: `IERC3009(tokenIn).receiveWithAuthorization(from, address(this), amount, ...); _settleSwap(zeroForOne, amount, tokenIn, from);` natspec: "Output always goes to `from`: a relayer cannot redirect it."; descriptor: "Swap {amount} from {from}", fields Pay, From, Valid before; case 7: 'Swap 21.37 zkUSD from Alice'.

findings.format: swap(address tokenIn, uint256 amount, address to)
findings.title: swap never shows the asset or amount the recipient receives; 'send to Bob' can read as sending zkUSD.
findings.reason: The pool derives the output token, which the guide explicitly treats as a spec limitation, not critical. Settlement sends exactly the displayed amount to the displayed recipient; the input token is correctly labelled “Pay.”
findings.quote: contracts/84532-0x9d02f341c2aefccf0a562f4db4111391dac2bd76/src/src/swap/ParSwapPool.sol, _settleSwap: `token1.safeTransfer(to, amount);` / `token0.safeTransfer(to, amount);`; constructor: `require(decimals0 == decimals1, DecimalsMismatch(decimals0, decimals1));`. cases/5.json screen: “Swap 21.37 zkUSD, send to Bob”, “Pay”: “21.37 zkUSD”, “To”: “Bob”. Registry .github/scripts/ai-review/prompt.md, checks §12: “an output token decided by a pool”; not_critical §3: “A party or a value the contract reads from storage or derives itself” is info.

findings.format: swapPushed(address tokenIn, uint256 amount, address to)
findings.title: swapPushed never shows the asset or amount the recipient receives.
findings.reason: The output token is derived by the pool, covered by the guide’s spec-limitation exclusion. The output amount equals the displayed amount, and the recipient is explicitly shown.
findings.quote: contracts/84532-0x9d02f341c2aefccf0a562f4db4111391dac2bd76/src/src/swap/ParSwapPool.sol, swapPushed: `_settleSwap(zeroForOne, amount, tokenIn, to);`; _settleSwap: `token1.safeTransfer(to, amount);` / `token0.safeTransfer(to, amount);`. cases/6.json screen: “Swap (pre-funded)”, “Pay”: “21.37 zkUSD”, “To”: “Bob”. Registry .github/scripts/ai-review/prompt.md, checks §12 classifies “an output token decided by a pool” as info; not_critical §2 excludes “A value that is shown through another field”.

findings.format: swapWithAuthorization(address tokenIn, uint256 amount, address from, uint256 validAfter, uint256 validBefore, bytes32 nonce, bytes signature)
findings.title: swapWithAuthorization does not show what token arrives, how much, or that `from` receives it.
findings.reason: The pool derives the output token and returns the displayed amount to the displayed owner, with no independently selectable output recipient. The missing explanation of the owner’s recipient role is a wording issue; the guide excludes derived outputs and values shown through another field from critical severity.
findings.quote: contracts/84532-0x9d02f341c2aefccf0a562f4db4111391dac2bd76/src/src/swap/ParSwapPool.sol, swapWithAuthorization: `_settleSwap(zeroForOne, amount, tokenIn, from);`; _settleSwap: `token1.safeTransfer(to, amount);` / `token0.safeTransfer(to, amount);`. cases/7.json screen: “Swap 21.37 zkUSD from Alice”, “Pay”: “21.37 zkUSD”, “From”: “Alice”. Registry .github/scripts/ai-review/prompt.md, not_critical §2: “A value that is shown through another field”; §3 includes “the recipient of a withdrawal that is always the account owner”; checks §12: “an output token decided by a pool” is info.
